references.text: Jesus applies the parable and urges using unrighteous mammon to make friends, so that they may be welcomed into 'the eternal dwellings' – [ref:Luk 16:9|Luke 16:9] expresses the same goal as the steward had: to be received into others' houses (οἴκους / σκηνάς).

Jesus' call to sell what one owns and give to the poor, thus securing a treasure in heaven that does not fade away, reflects the steward's strategy of ensuring his future through generosity – [ref:Luk 12:33|Luke 12:33].

The context for the steward's plan: he has been accused of wasting his master's property and knows he will lose his position – [ref:Luk 16:1-3|Luke 16:1-3] provides the background for his wise action.
The steward's plan in verse 4 is carried out in practice by summoning his master's debtors and reducing their debts – [ref:Luk 16:5-7|Luke 16:5-7].
Proverbs give advice to act quickly and wisely when in a difficult situation, which reflects the steward's decisive action to secure his future – [ref:Ordsp 6:1-3|Proverbs 6:1-3].

The Lord's praise of the unrighteous steward because he acted wisely confirms that the plan in verse 4 was successful – 'the people of this world are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the people of the light' – [ref:Luk 16:8|Luke 16:8].
Paul urges believers to be careful how they live and to make the most of every opportunity, which reflects the steward's wise use of the limited time he had left – [ref:Ef 5:15-16|Ephesians 5:15-16].
Jesus' words about being as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves point to the same kind of wisdom the steward showed in his plan – [ref:Matt 10:16|Matthew 10:16].
